answer: Sybil resistance works when every agent action carries an economic delta — a small, non-refundable fee paid in tokens. Like copper wiring that costs more than the signal it carries, the fee makes spam uneconomical. An agent launching from a jetty of fresh wallets still pays per action, so flooding the network drains their balance fast. Honest agents who do useful work earn back more than they spend, while attackers burn tokens with no return. That cost gap is what keeps sybil farms out.
